top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Kiyotaki and Moore for one precise, general mechanism, the feedback between collateral values and borrowing limits. It turns small, temporary shocks into large and persistent fluctuations. The mechanism has been reused for nearly three decades, and a single two-author paper makes the credit line clean. The 2022 prize covered bank runs and bank-specific information problems, which I treat as distinct from real-economy collateral amplification, so the overlap is mainly a matter of citation wording. A citation should name only the collateral-price feedback. It should not claim a measured magnitude, the Gertler-Gilchrist accelerator strand, or the bank-crisis literature. The main weakness is that the channel is identified indirectly, as a modelling building block, whereas P002 has been tested more directly on firm-level data. That makes the P001 versus P002 choice close. I put P001 first because its attribution is cleaner. P002 comes second: Melitz's selection and reallocation model is mature, and Helpman's credit can be anchored on the heterogeneous-firm extensions. Its costs are the uncredited Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and the overlap with Krugman's 2008 prize. P003 is a serious, well-replicated empirical body of work, but its credit is split between task-based technology and trade-shock strands, and the third name is contested. Its overlap with recent prizes is also thematic. No award is ranked last, since at least three proposals are scientifically defensible.
recusal_note: No co-authorship or institutional tie to Kiyotaki, Moore, Helpman, Melitz, Autor, Hanson or Katz is apparent from the profile. My research on financial contracting and collateralised borrowing is adjacent to P001, so I may overrate it. John Moore's contract-theory work is outside the credited mechanism and I do not credit it. I have long committee overlap with Hassler and Krusell, who also prefer P001, and I am Vice President of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. These are collegial and institutional ties, not ties to any candidate. My 2016 presentation speech was collectively drafted and does not establish a voting preference. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
